name: Enjin
rootCause: unprotected registry reinitialization, manager takeover. Lost: 5,231,353 ENJ (~$142K)

descriptions.text: unprotected registry reinitialization, manager takeover. Lost: 5,231,353 ENJ (~$142K)

Enjin’s legacy ERC-1155 Crypto Items platform on Ethereum was exploited. The attacker used a storage-layout mismatch in delegate-call adapters plus an unprotected initialize function to take over the Managed Delegate Proxy via DELEGATECALL. After gaining manager privileges, they registered a malicious adapter, transferred NFTs from about 52 wallets without approval, and melted them to redeem the backing ENJ from the reserve, draining approximately 5.24 million ENJ .

On August 25, 2026, an attacker exploited a storage-layout mismatch and missing approval checks in Enjin's Ethereum-based Crypto Items platform, draining approximately 5.24 million ENJ (~$142,000,$162,000) from the platform reserve via a single Ethereum transaction. The attacker used a malicious transfer adapter to bypass standard authorization safeguards and melted stolen NFTs for their ENJ backing. A vulnerable per-item transfer adapter lacked owner-approval verification due to a storage-slot collision and unprotected initialization. This allowed unauthorized transfers of ENJ-backed Crypto Items, leading to their melting and reserve fund drain.
